workspaceNote: This workspace does not produce a weighted score or a winner. It helps you record, stage by stage, what each agency actually said or committed to in writing, so you can compare candidates on facts you wrote down rather than on the impression left by the meeting.

stages.label: Initial call
stages.purpose: Tests whether the agency is diagnosing your business or reciting a script it uses on every caller.

items.question: What do you need to know about my business before you can design anything?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: The agency asks about audience, offer, competitors and what is currently not working, before showing any visual concept.
items.redFlag: The agency opens with a mockup or a visual style before asking a single question about your business.

items.question: How will we know, in measurable terms, whether this project worked?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: A concrete answer referencing enquiries, bookings, rankings, load time or another measurable outcome tied to your goals.
items.redFlag: A vague answer about looking professional or modern, with no measurable definition of success.

items.question: Who owns the code, the domain and the hosting account once the project is finished?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: A direct, specific answer naming the accounts and confirming they transfer to you.
items.redFlag: Vagueness, deflection, or a change of subject when ownership comes up this early.

stages.label: Proposal review
stages.purpose: Tests whether the agency's written commitments are specific enough to hold anyone to later.

items.question: What, specifically, does 'SEO included' cover on this project?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: An itemised list: page structure, metadata, sitemap, structured data, or similar named technical elements.
items.redFlag: 'SEO included' appears as a phrase with no technical element named anywhere in the document.

items.question: What exactly is excluded from this price, and what would trigger an extra charge?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: A written exclusions list (for example copywriting, extra language versions, third-party licences) stated up front.
items.redFlag: A single all-in price with no exclusions list, or exclusions only mentioned after signing.

items.question: What happens to the timeline and the price if my content arrives later than planned?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: A stated policy: revised timeline, defined revision rounds, and how delay on either side is handled.
items.redFlag: No written process for delay, or 'unlimited revisions' marketed with no explanation of how it protects the schedule.

stages.label: Reference check
stages.purpose: Tests whether the outcomes the agency claims are verifiable independently of its own account.

items.question: Can I contact two or three clients directly, without you present on the call?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: Direct contact details for findable, independent references, or an honest 'not yet published' from a young agency.
items.redFlag: Only quotes with no findable source, or refusal to provide any contactable reference at all.

items.question: What is a live, comparable site I can test myself with a free page-speed tool?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: A live URL you can independently run through a tool such as Google PageSpeed Insights.
items.redFlag: No testable live reference offered, or performance described only in adjectives such as 'blazing fast'.

items.question: What happened the last time a client needed a small change months after launch?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: A specific, concrete account of turnaround time and cost for a real post-launch change.
items.redFlag: A generic reassurance with no specific example, timeframe or cost mentioned.

stages.label: Contract review
stages.purpose: Tests what actually happens once the relationship ends, whether that is well or badly.

items.question: Which specific accounts transfer to my name, and when?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: The contract names the domain registrar, hosting account, CMS admin login and source repository explicitly.
items.redFlag: Ownership is implied verbally but the contract's rights clause says something different or stays silent.

items.question: Is this a one-time invoice or a recurring contract, and how do I cancel it?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: A clear billing model and, if recurring, an explicit notice period with no automatic-renewal surprise.
items.redFlag: An automatically renewing annual contract with a narrow cancellation window, or an exit fee to release your own domain.

items.question: Is there a written response-time commitment for support after launch, or only a verbal one?
items.whatGoodLooksLike: A written response time and a clear, upfront cost for small changes after launch.
items.redFlag: 'We're always here for you' with no written commitment, or maintenance pricing disclosed only after signing.

disclaimer: All notes in this workspace are entered by you and stored only in your own browser. No agency names are pre-filled, no Weissmann-specific values are hidden in the data, and nothing you type is sent anywhere. This workspace does not replace your own legal review of any contract.
